scope: Eight Maine Saco research records; excludes the separate New Hampshire family and protected comparison/winner cohorts
finding: Endpoint proliferation hid material source-binding, distance and dam-boundary errors. Similarity alone would not have found or corrected them. This is evidence of product-quality defects, not proof of Google's ranking cause.

sources.readVia: Current browser inventory and official www1 mirror
sources.supports: Exact stored coordinates are facility-area anchors. The 44.03800,-70.98170 entry is in Fryeburg, not Denmark. Front Street's state tidal facility is distinct from Saco's freshwater municipal ramp. Dayton has two different Brookfield facilities.
sources.limits: An inventory establishes neither a surveyed wet entry nor continuous passage between launches.

sources.supports: Named Swan's Falls–Brownfield overnight trip, approximately two paddling days in average mid-summer conditions, and prearranged shuttle advice.
sources.limits: Duration is conditional; it supplies no recreational discharge cutoff.

sources.supports: Downstream sequence Swan's Falls, Canal Bridge, Walker's Bridge / Route 302, Walker's Rips, Lovewell Pond and Brownfield Bridge. Approximate reference markers: Canal near 3, Brownfield near 18.
sources.inference: About fifteen remaining reference miles for Canal–Brownfield, subtracting 3 from 18. Not a surveyed track or permission to use every intermediate bank.

sources.supports: Council manages Swan's Falls, Canal Bridge and Brownfield Bridge; vehicles left there need parking passes.
sources.limits: Facility ownership and management differ. A parking pass does not grant camping rights.

sources.supports: Independent monitoring-site geography places Canal Bridge near 44.06759,-70.94893, below Swan Falls near 44.03883,-70.98034 and Brownfield's Route 160 bridge near 43.95551,-70.88266.
sources.limits: Monitoring coordinates are not boat landing coordinates or a public-access permission source. Used together with the current launch inventory and Council map, not to relocate any endpoint.

sources.supports: A real source-named Route 302–Route 160 / Lovewell Pond paddle exists in Sanborn WMA.
sources.limits: The article does not georeference the stored Canal / Swan's Falls pins or validate their four-mile endpoint ordering. Preserve its original source URL; do not dismiss the named trip itself or silently repin it.

sources.supports: Operator distinguishes Hiram, Bonny Eagle, West Buxton, Bar Mills, Skelton and lower hydroelectric projects.
sources.limits: A listed portage amenity or proposed decommissioning does not establish a complete lawful staged trip, current passage or a removed dam. Operational minimum flows are not paddling cutoffs.

sources.supports: Front Street is below head of tide with a low-water ramp warning; Meeting House Eddy / Marblehead is a separate downstream state ramp.
sources.limits: The facility descriptions do not verify the stored five-mile/2–4-hour tidal estimate.
Predicted height or high/low-water time is not a tidal-current, slack-water or safe-passage prediction.

decisions.reason: Source-named overnight trip; correct existing facility label to Swan's Falls and distance/time to about eighteen reference miles / two days. Preserve original ID, slug, endpoint IDs and coordinates. Cornish remains a downstream proxy. Legacy line is fifty disconnected named-fallback fragments with a recorded 16385-foot endpoint snap; withhold line and GPX while keeping facility planning available.

Same upper corridor, gauge, rapid and finish; alternate Canal Bridge start. Correct facility name and derive approximately fifteen reference miles. Retain its connected network-traced planning corridor and exact saved-plan anchor.

Separate below-head-of-tide setting, source-bound Front Street and Marblehead facilities, tidal-current/landing decisions and distinct station context. Preserve connected network-traced corridor. Explicitly qualify unverified catalog distance and withdraw unsupported travel time.
Stored Canal-to-Swan's Falls order conflicts with the downstream map and source-named crossing identity. Do not reverse or repin automatically.
Unreviewed upper-to-lower dam-transfer chain; the old twenty-six-mile/full-day instructions do not establish passage.
Longer sibling combination crosses that same unresolved dam system; generic multi-day wording did not cure it.
Upper-to-lower dam system and distinct upstream freshwater municipal finish; old thirty-one-mile/full-day instructions do not establish passage.
Freshwater Dayton to below-head-of-tide Marblehead requires an unreviewed staged passage through separate river settings; exact launch side also needs verification.

preservation: Keep all eight research identities and original source URLs. Do not move coordinates or remove the six NH trips. Retain five held-trip legacy assets; archive the one misleading Swan's Falls line before replacing its public asset with an explicit geometry hold. All other canonical route assets and unrelated public records must remain identical.
